notes.title: The long way around.
notes.summary: Rail trails, quieter roads, and the freedom to follow a promising turn.
paragraphs: Cycling is one of my favourite ways to explore. A long trail changes the pace of a place: there is time to notice a bridge, a shoreline, or a little side road that would disappear through a car window.
The BLT trail toward Hubbards and the Confederation Trail on Prince Edward Island are part of that interest. Here in British Columbia, there is always another route to connect.
This section is a place for future ride notes, photographs, and things worth returning to. I am more interested in what a route feels like than in turning every outing into a performance chart.

notes.title: The interesting bits in between.
notes.summary: Quiet corridors, reflections, old infrastructure, and the scenes most people walk past.
paragraphs: I am drawn to the atmosphere of in-between places: a quiet public corridor, a building after the crowds have gone, a reflection that makes a familiar street feel unfamiliar.

Photography gives that curiosity somewhere to go. Sometimes the interesting part is the light; sometimes it is a composition that takes a second look to understand. Polaroids, older formats, and simple in-camera experiments all fit that way of seeing.

Urban exploration, for me, starts with attention and respect for a place. There is plenty to find from public streets and permitted spaces without publishing sensitive locations or crossing a boundary.
This will grow into a collection of observations and photographs. For now, it is an invitation to look a little longer.

notes.title: A web worth keeping.
notes.summary: Personal websites, community networks, and the pleasure of making something small.
paragraphs: The part of the internet I enjoy most feels made by people. A personal homepage, a useful little script, a local community network, or an email exchange can have more character than a polished feed.
That is why I keep coming back to Linux, self-hosting, and the indie web. They make it possible to understand the tools I use and to build a corner that behaves the way I want.
The same curiosity connects computers with exploration: follow a path, find out how a thing works, leave a useful note for the next person.
The workshop holds the technical details. This site holds the wider picture: what I am making, what catches my eye, and the places the curiosity leads.
